name: NFT Trader BatchSwap counterparty reentrancy
summary: BatchSwap.closeSwapIntent() settles the creator's side of a swap with an ERC-721 safeTransferFrom before the counterparty side, and has no reentrancy guard. The attacker re-entered from onERC721Received and called editCounterPart() to point the open swap at any address that still held an ERC-721 approval to the contract, so settlement then pulled that address's token to the attacker.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0xf47d9ba7a1d6818b73b3936ee83e718ad4f2e24e6d14a1b93d856c6ded1dcb16 both at the deployment block 12505457 and at block 18797419, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

143 distinct NFTs were pulled from approval-holding victims through this contract between blocks 18797420 and 18799856. Only the 12 BAYC and 13 MAYC are valued. Unit values are the median single-item marketplace fill for each collection over blocks 18790000-18804000, taken only from transactions carrying a Seaport OrderFulfilled or Blur execution event and measured as the payment received by the seller, with every campaign address excluded: BAYC 26.300 ETH from 34 sales, MAYC 5.190 ETH from 85 sales. Those medians are converted at the DefiLlama ETH price for the incident timestamp. The remaining 118 NFTs across 25 collections (World of Women, Hashmasks, HERO, VeeFriends, 0N1, HAPE, OCMonk, CloneX, PartyBears, Azuki, Doodles and others) are not valued, so the figure is a conservative floor; press coverage of the whole NFT Trader event reports close to USD 3 million across both exploited swap contracts. The 26 BAYC and 9 MAYC taken through the separate contract 0x13d8faf4a690f5ae52e2d2c52938d1167057b9af are recorded under eip155:1:0x906d06acd236c48a8c8708d7dc50d968b8faad7c7c393e7c01549adf4922b180 and are not counted here. Recovery is excluded: Yuga Labs and Boring Security later paid a 120 ETH bounty and the main exploiter returned 36 BAYC and 18 MAYC.
